literal: Arrow is cruel, lute curve is good; thus like that, by the nature resulting from action, understand.
translation: An arrow is straight but cruel, while a lute is curved but sweet. In the same way, judge people by the nature of their deeds, not their appearance.
modern: கணை நேராக இருந்தாலும் கொடியது, யாழின் வளைவு கோணலாக இருந்தாலும் இனிமையானது. அதுபோலவே மக்களின் தோற்றத்தை வைத்து அல்லாமல் அவர்கள் செய்யும் செயல்களின் தன்மையை வைத்து அவர்களைப் புரிந்துகொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet teaches that outward appearance does not reveal true character. An arrow is perfectly straight but brings harm, whereas the curved neck of a lute produces sweet music. Therefore, one must judge people by the nature of their actions rather than their physical form or outward guise. The word 'koṭitu' means cruel or crooked, contrasting with 'cevvitu' which means upright or good. The poet plays on the visual straightness of the arrow and the physical curve of the lute to show that true straightness lies in good deeds.
